current_dh_model.note: Clamp changes the result only slightly. The dominant error is not caused by J7 exceeding the 90 degree planning limit.

diagnostics.translation_only_is_not_enough: A fixed SDK-FK translation still leaves about 17 cm RMS residual.
diagnostics.rigid_transform_is_not_enough: An arbitrary rigid transform from current FK points to SDK points still leaves about 11.5 cm RMS residual.
diagnostics.not_tcp_offset: The data compare flange-to-flange positions, so the gripper TCP offset is not the primary source.

sample_3_4_5_j1_sweep.description: Samples 3, 4, and 5 keep joints 2-7 nearly fixed while J1 changes. SDK flange z stays constant, and current FK flange z also stays constant, but the horizontal radius differs strongly.

best_signed_axis_permutation.note: Axis permutation improves over raw FK but remains far from usable.

coarse_joint_mapping_scan.note: This coarse scan is diagnostic only. It does not produce an acceptable correction.

conclusion.root_cause_likely: The current simulation FK uses DH zero points, joint signs, and/or base/flange frame conventions that do not match the SDK-reported flange pose.
conclusion.safety_decision: Do not use current FK/TCP z for real-robot table clearance or collision checks until an SDK-compatible FK chain is implemented.

recommended_next_steps: Create an SDK-compatible kinematics calibration layer: q_sdk -> q_dh plus base/flange frame transform.
Fit this layer against the manual flange samples and validate on held-out poses.
Until residuals are below about 20-30 mm, keep real-robot motion based on SDK Cartesian feedback and conservative manual waypoints rather than current offline FK.
